newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks end higher on speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks end higher on speculative trade.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended higher on Wednesday mainly on speculative activity linked to the February 3 general elections, dealers said.

The Karachi 100-share index gained 14.86 points, or 1.04 percent, to end at 1,444.49 amid 141 gainers and 74 losers. Turnover rose to 25.431 million shares from just 706,000 on Tuesday's when only a brief trading was done because of a general strike in the city.
"Most activity was generated by speculators hoping that (pro-business former prime minister) Nawaz Sharif will win the elections," dealer Sameera Manto said.
Dealers said the index would rise in the near-term as sentiment was positive.

Dewan Salman Fibres rose 3.0 rupees to 34.75, Hub Power 0.35 to 36.35, PTCL 0.50 to 28.40, ICI Pakistan 0.95 to 18.90 and Lever Brothers 10 to 660. Pak State Oil fell 5.0 rupees to 279 and Essa Cement 0.25 to 10.50.
